title: Can You Get a Bonded Title With Bad Credit?
excerpt: Yes. Bonds under $30,000 are issued without a credit check at all, and above that a poor score affects the rate rather than the answer.
metaDescription: Bad credit and bonded titles: why no credit check applies under $30,000, what changes above it, and what the surety is actually assessing.

body.text: Yes. For the overwhelming majority of applicants the question never comes up, because bonds under $30,000 are issued with no credit check at all. Since the bond amount is a multiple of the vehicle's value, a $30,000 bond covers a vehicle worth $15,000 to $20,000 depending on the state, which is most of the vehicles anyone needs a bonded title for.
Why credit matters so little here

A surety bond is not a loan. Nobody is lending you money, so there is no repayment to assess. The surety is guaranteeing that if a legitimate owner appears and proves a better claim, they will be compensated. See Cornell's [definition of a surety](https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/surety) for the legal shape of that arrangement.

What the surety is pricing is the chance that somebody turns up with a better claim to this vehicle, which has almost nothing to do with your credit score and everything to do with the vehicle's history.

On larger bonds credit can be reviewed. Even then it usually affects the rate rather than the outcome, and a poor score does not by itself mean a decline. If your vehicle is valuable enough to need a bond that size, call rather than assume.
These matter far more than a credit score:

items: A vehicle reported stolen, or with an unresolved lien on record.
A title branded salvage or junk in the national record.
A previous claim against a bond you held.
Evidence of ownership that does not hold together.

body.text: Most of these are visible in the [national title record](https://vehiclehistory.bja.ojp.gov/) before you apply, which is worth checking first.

The premium is 1.5% of the bond amount with a $100 minimum, the same figure regardless of credit on bonds under $30,000. A $12,000 bond costs $180 whether your score is 800 or 500, and [what a bonded title costs](/how-much-does-a-bonded-title-cost) covers the fees the state adds on top.
If you are still working out the coverage you need, [how your bond amount is determined](/how-your-bond-amount-is-determined) explains the multiplier and the valuation methods states accept.
